newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak govt prepares economic trade package.
newsitem.headline: Slovak govt prepares economic trade package.

text.p: Slovakia said on Tuesday it was preparing a package of unspecified economic measures which are widely believed to be a response to the imposition of general import restrictions by the neighbouring Czech Republic.
"Full details of the package will be announced on Wednesday by Finance Minister Sergei Kozlik," government spokeswoman Ludmila Bulakova told a news conference during a regular government session.
"They are related to changes in external economic conditions," Bulakova said without elaborating.

Last Wednesday, the Czechs announced a package of economic measures to revive the economy. One measure was a requirement on all importers of consumer and agricultural goods to deposit sums equal to 20 percent of the value of their imports in non-interest bearing accounts at Czech banks.
Slovakia claims that the measure, which came into effect on Monday and applies to all countries without exception, will hurt its exports.
Bulakova added that the Slovak ambassador to the Czech Republic Ivan Mjartan, who was recalled for consultations earlier this month, had attended discussions about the matter.

Mjartan was recalled in the wake of a row between the Czech Republic and Slovakia after Czech President Vaclav Havel was reportedly quoted in a French newspaper as describing Slovak Prime Minster Vladimir Meciar as "paranoid."
